common_name: Eclipse Hydrangea (First Dark-Leaf Bigleaf Mophead Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in morning sun with afternoon shade; Eclipse is notable for dark purple foliage that holds its color even in warm climates, paired with pink-and-cream mophead blooms.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil, giving morning sun and afternoon shade to protect the dark foliage from scorch in hot climates. Eclipse was bred as the first bigleaf hydrangea with true dark purple leaves that retain color throughout the summer and into fall rather than fading to green, setting its red-pink mophead blooms with creamy white centers against near-black foliage for strong landscape contrast. Its mounded, well-branched habit holds blooms upright and works well as a focal point, in mixed borders, or in large containers. Like other bigleaf hydrangeas, avoid hard pruning in fall or early spring since flower buds form on the previous season's wood.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Spring Sizzle is among the earliest-blooming panicle hydrangeas, opening green-white and progressing through blushed pink to red even in warm regions.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade. Spring Sizzle flowers notably earlier than most panicle hydrangea cultivars, opening green-white conical panicles in early summer that progress through blushed pink to a strong red even where summer heat normally delays or washes out color on other paniculata types. Its upright, vase-shaped habit and strong stems hold the flower heads well above the dark green foliage without flopping, making it useful for hedges and foundation plantings as well as cut flowers. Like other H. paniculata selections it blooms on new wood, so prune hard in late winter or early spring to maximize the following season's bloom.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; DreamScape opens with vibrant rosy-pink mophead blooms that mature through greyed-red toward tan by season's end, on sturdy, lodging-resistant stems.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade depending on climate. DreamScape is a native smooth hydrangea selection valued for its vibrant rosy-pink, 8 to 10 inch mophead flower heads that open in late spring to early summer and gradually shift through greyed-red tones toward tan as the season advances, extending the display. Its strong branches resist lodging far better than older seedling-grown smooth hydrangeas, holding the full, mounded habit without flopping in wind or rain. Like other smooth hydrangeas it blooms on new wood, so cut it back hard in early spring to encourage vigorous growth and abundant, pollinator-friendly blooms the same year.
